decision: No blocker to the exact narrow read-only diagnostic. It cannot classify an unmatched PID or establish a benign cleanup result.
checks: Entire5257-byte source reviewed. It opens only the fixed failed-inspection qemu-stderr.txt path read-only with no-follow and canonical/ordinary-file checks; it creates no file, process or signal and invokes no recovery action.

Reads are bounded64MiB and4097-byte line fragments, with at most64 matching target-PID projections. It hashes all consumed bytes and checks device/inode/size/mtime/ctime plus final path identity; overlong-line projection limitations are explicitly reported.
Output includes only source identity/hash, numeric fields from exact known native worker diagnostics, counts and the latest numeric pool summary. No raw stderr or guest serial line is printed.

All five PID-pattern families and the pool-summary format were checked against the reconstructed exact native-el0.c. That source matches SHA-256 a6c9a6110f6a34ddfdab5a4ce29bd1ecf176692de9f1d4f7546078734b0ca598 and Git blob180bf260f60d878b0b579819de5115cfd5fc6085 from the qualified-source record.

The constructor assigns factory_pid after fork without logging that PID. The observer therefore correctly states that missing matching diagnostics do not classify target13344 or establish a benign exit; it does not conflate worker, factory or unrelated PID identities.

The3153-byte command shell-parses to a single isolated Python invocation and its embedded payload reconstructs byte-for-byte to the reviewed source. No broad tests or phone/GitHub actions were performed by this reviewer.
limits: This review covers the diagnostic source and command, not its future physical output.
A numeric-PID match without start ticks does not independently establish the historical process identity.
The failed inspection and forced-descendant rejection remain unchanged; no retry or downstream execution is released.
